scouting_result.scout_verdict:
At 28 years old, your physical composition of 181cm and 83kg provides the ideal leverage and power-to-weight ratio to anchor a synchronized crew. You have clearly identified that your best performance emerges from the collaborative intensity of team dynamics; in the shell, this translates into a seamless, unified rhythm where your individual output is amplified by the collective. Your capacity to enter an internal, meditative state of flow is your greatest asset here, allowing you to sustain high-intensity effort while remaining perfectly attuned to the stroke cadence of your teammates, ensuring the boat glides with maximum efficiency through every phase of the race.

In the adaptive sphere, your pathway transitions to the ASM1x classification—a category for athletes with a trunk function impairment who rely on upper-body strength to drive the boat. This classification represents a significant shift in technical focus; without the use of leg drive, the meditative rhythm you value must be reconstructed through precise upper-body mechanics and core stabilization. Embracing the challenge of the ASM1x allows you to explore the same pursuit of fluid, rhythmic mastery you enjoy in team settings, but as a solo endeavor where every nuance of the blade entry is entirely under your control.

While your rowing profile leverages your need for team cohesion, your secondary path as a 'Road Machine' highlights your capability for high-efficiency, individual technical performance. This path demands a shift from the rhythmic internal flow of the water to the external, tactical mastery of the road. Here, your endurance is refined into a calculated display of efficiency, where you are constantly measuring output against the changing resistance of the terrain and the tactical maneuvers of your competitors. It is a disciplined, solitary pursuit that tests your ability to maintain composure during high-speed, long-distance segments.

Your adaptive expression lies within the H3 handcycling classification, which serves athletes with lower-limb impairment who maintain good trunk stability. This discipline provides a striking contrast to the team-focused rowing pathway; it requires a sophisticated understanding of mechanical efficiency and aerodynamic positioning. Unlike the meditative flow found in the boat, the H3 road race is an aggressive, analytical challenge that demands you treat your body and cycle as a singular, optimized machine. This shift allows you to apply your deep aerobic base to an entirely different mechanical environment, providing a rigorous test of your technical precision on the open road.
